snippet.title: How to decrease your electricity bill with smart meters
snippet.description:
The truth about smart meters replacing your manual meter. Here's why. For over a century, a physical or manual meter outside your home would determine how much electricity you've used in kilowatt hours. Someone would come around every three months to record your usage.
Then, your electricity bill was calculated by charging you a flat rate of, let's say, 25 cents per kilowatt hour. Now, smart meters can output your energy usage every 30 minutes to your energy retailer. This means your bill can be calculated based on time of use.

With smart meters, you could be charged 40 cents per kilowatt hour during peak periods. However, the benefit of smart meters is that during off-peak periods, you can be charged as little as 10 cents. So, you're incentivised to use your electricity at off-peak times, which can save you money, but only if you have the flexibility to do so.
